title: The same answer serves conditional futures: given that the agent would so act, it must so act under the condition
source_text: LXII. Sed quod vir Doctissimus de absolute futuris dicendum existimat, non minori cum ratione ad conditionate futura applicari potest. Dicam enim eodem modo Deum certo praevidere quod libere futurum esset sub aliqua conditione; quia licet causa libera posset aliter agere, nec ista conditio illi necessitatem agendi imponeret, nihilominus reipsa sic ageret. Ex hypothesi autem quod sic ageret, necesse est ut sic agat posita conditione, & ita res est quae possit a Deo certo sciri.
pass_a_gloss: LXII. But what the most learned man judges must be said of things absolutely future, can be applied with no less reason to things conditionally future. For I will say in the same way that God certainly foresees what would be freely future under some condition; because although the free cause could act otherwise, nor would that condition impose on it a necessity of acting, nevertheless in fact it would so act. But on the hypothesis that it would so act, it is necessary that it so act the condition being posited, & thus it is a thing which can be certainly known by God.
pass_b_english: What that very learned man thinks must be said of absolute futures can be applied with no less reason to conditional futures. I will say in the same way that God foresees with certainty what would freely happen under some condition.

He foresees it because, although the free cause could act otherwise and the condition would not force it to act, it would in fact act in this way. On the hypothesis that it would act in this way, it must act so once the condition is in place. So it is something God can know with certainty.
